Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

### Correction on the root cause

My earlier comments pointed at `packages/llm/src/route/executor.ts` as the injection point. That was wrong, and testing a build with the change in place showed traces were still disconnected. Two things are actually going on:

**1. No propagator is registered.** `tracingLayer()` in `packages/core/src/observability/otlp.ts` sets a global context manager but never sets a propagator. `propagation.inject()` falls back to a no-op propagator when none is registered, so it writes nothing to the carrier. Confirmed by logging the carrier during a live run: `carrier={}` on every request. This is the primary reason no trace headers are sent, and it would defeat an injection call placed anywhere.

**2. `executor.ts` is not on the request path.** AI SDK providers issue their HTTP requests through the provider `fetch` wrapper in `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` (~line 1822), not the Effect HTTP client in `packages/llm/src/route/executor.ts`. Injection has to go in the fetch wrapper to cover providers.

With a propagator registered and the injection in the fetch wrapper, the same live session produces:

```
carrier={"traceparent":"00-eb775c51c6fdf39a427732baa9da8178-28eae3b144d52dad-01"}
```

and the gateway server span lands in the client trace:

```
ai.streamText.doStream       [INTERNAL]  opencode   span=28eae3b144d52dad
  └─ chat openai-gpt-5.4     [SERVER]    gateway    parent=28eae3b144d52dad
```

PR #49046 has been updated with this approach: 2 files, 30 lines.

> Your payload is the right one for api.deepseek.com, but I don't think `variants()` is reached for these models: `provider.ts:1310` does `ProviderTransform.reasoningVariants(model, base) ?? ProviderTransform.variants(base)`, and because models.dev declares `reasoning_options` for `deepseek-v4-*`, `reasoningVariants` returns low/high/max and short-circuits the fallback. Worth checking against your build in case I've misread it.
> 
> Your `model.providerID === "deepseek"` guard was the right instinct — I counted ~63 models across ~30 providers that would match on the model id alone, and zen turns out to need a different payload again (it ignores `thinking` and accepts `reasoning_effort: "none"`).
> 
> I opened #46181, which moves this into `reasoningVariants` and keeps your provider scoping. Happy to close mine if you'd prefer to move yours instead.

I am fine with closing mine. I don’t think there was a bug when I wrote the first version because I managed to get it working but I haven’t tested it and the code flow probably changed.

Independent corroboration from a downstream harness (opencode 1.18.30, Linux apptainer/HPC host, 47 opencode processes, load ~14).

A single assistant message dispatched **three `task` (subagent) tool calls in one step**. The fastest subagent completed normally; **the two slower ones returned bare `Tool execution aborted`** — no `task_id`, no partial output, no artifacts. Re-running those two **sequentially, one per message, both succeeded**.

That matches your "one fast + one slow co-dispatched" condition exactly, and adds one data point on the transport axis: the aborted calls here were **`task` tool calls** (not `bash`/`webfetch`/MCP), so the race appears to be transport-agnostic in the same way your repros are.

Two honest caveats on our side:

1. Our runtime log has **no abort event for this window at all** — the ~5452 lines covering it are all INFO, and a census of `message=` kinds shows no task/abort lifecycle event. So we could not confirm the mechanism from outside; we are citing your 250 ms cleanup finding as the leading explanation, not as our own verification.
2. Because the failing call never returned, the parent had **no `task_id` to resume from** — consistent with #44791. Serial re-run was the only recovery.

If it's useful, our notes (including the negative logging evidence and the repro shape) are in a write-up we can share on request. Thanks for pulling the root cause out of the generic symptom pile — the step-boundary framing (don't stamp while same-step calls are still running) is what we'd expect to fix our case too.

### Consolidated status: one click clears this PR — and three separate clocks are now running against it

This replaces my earlier notes with the current mechanics, two measured counter-examples, and the deadlines. Short version: **nothing is wrong with the change, and no review decision is pending — the PR is waiting on a workflow approval that only a maintainer can give, and an automated cleanup job will close it on 2026-09-19 if that approval does not arrive.**

#### 1. Every required check on this branch is a check that never ran

Ruleset `19434226` (active, applies to `refs/heads/v2`) requires exactly five contexts — `unit (linux)`, `unit (windows)`, `e2e (linux)`, `e2e (windows)`, `typecheck`. All five are produced by the `test` workflow, and on this branch they are `completed / action_required` since 2026-08-25, i.e. they were queued and never approved, so they have never executed:

- `test` → run 32837016989, `action_required`
- `typecheck` → run 32837016988, `action_required`

The only checks that do report are `check-standards` / `check-compliance`, which come from `pull_request_target` and are not in the required list. `gh pr checks` lists only runs that executed, so the PR reads as "CI green, blocked on review" when in fact the required contexts have simply never been produced.

#### 2. The gate is per-contributor, and a past merge does not clear it

I checked this against other contributors rather than assuming:

| contributor | merged PRs in this repo | their fork PR's runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `argszero` (me) | **0** | `action_required`, never executed |
| `mynameistito` | 1 (merged 2026-01-28) | still `action_required` on #49069 (2026-09-14) |
| `OpeOginni` | **83** | all five required contexts reported → #48952 **merged** 2026-09-14T14:28Z |

So being an occasional contributor is not enough (`mynameistito` still needs approval after a merge eight months ago), while an established contributor's fork PR runs unattended. The pattern I observe is that the flag clears when a run is approved **once** for that contributor, after which their later runs execute automatically — which is why this is a one-time cost, not a standing burden.

#### 3. A merge does not actually require those checks

Two live examples from the last 24 hours:

- **#48952** (fork → `v2`, author `OpeOginni`) was merged with the required `unit (windows)` **failing** — so a maintainer bypass of the ruleset is evidently acceptable when the change is understood.
- **#49061** (fork, author `Yedigaryan`) targets the branch `retry-empty-response` rather than `v2`; the v2 ruleset does not apply to that base, so the same check gap does not block it.

In other words, neither "approve the runs" nor "merge directly" is novel here — either one ends this.

#### 4. The automated cleanup deadline

This repository's *Automated PR Cleanup* job closes PRs that are older than one month with fewer than 2 positive reactions. This PR was created 2026-08-19T15:16Z and has 0 positive reactions, so it becomes eligible on **2026-09-19T15:16Z**. My other PR, #43282 (created 2026-08-18T19:02Z), becomes eligible on **2026-09-18T19:02Z**. Comments do not reset that clock.

For scale: `GET /repos/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs?status=action_required` reports **5,687** runs awaiting approval repo-wide as of today.

#### 5. What I am asking for

Either of these works, and both take one action:

1. **Approve and run** the pending `test` run on this branch — one click, and per the pattern above it also covers everything I open later; or
2. **Merge this PR directly** — it is conflict-free against `v2` right now (`mergeable: MERGEABLE`; the `BLOCKED` state is only the missing contexts from §1).
